nodes.name: PtPd-HEA Solvothermal Synthesis
nodes.procedure: High-entropy alloys were synthesized via a simple slow-dropping method. The synthesis process commenced with the addition of 20 mL of ethylene glycol (EG) to a 100 mL three-necked flask. An inert atmosphere was subsequently established within the flask through three cycles of vacuum evacuation followed by argon gas (Ar) purging, and the resulting solution was designated as Solution A. Solution A was then heated to 200°C. To prepare Solution B, 0.025 mmol each of Pt(acac)₂, Pd(acac)₂, Co(acac)₂, Ni(acac)₂, and Cu(acac)₂ were dissolved in 20 mL of EG, and the mixture was homogenized via ultrasonication. Solution B was added dropwise to Solution A at a constant rate of 1 mL min⁻¹ using a peristaltic pump. Upon completion of the dropwise addition, the resulting mixture was maintained at 200°C for an additional 40 min to facilitate the complete reduction of the metal elements. Throughout the entire synthesis procedure, a rotational speed of 800 rpm was maintained. After cooling to room temperature, the mixture underwent centrifugal washing with ethanol and acetone that had been purified by using Ar. The final product, PtPd-HEA, was obtained by drying in a vacuum oven at 60°C for 6 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: All catalysts show face-centered cubic (FCC) structure with diffraction peaks at 2θ ≈ 42°, 48°, 69°, 84° corresponding to (111), (200), (220), (311) planes. No characteristic peaks for individual metals indicating single-phase alloy structure without phase segregation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern (Figure 1a) confirms that all catalysts are HEAs with a face-centered cubic (FCC) structure, showing four diffraction peaks at 2θ of approximately 42, 48, 69, and 84°, corresponding to the (111), (200), (220), and (311) planes.

nodes.characterization_summary: PtPd-HEA nanoparticles have average size of 9.5 ± 1.2 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images of PtPd-HEA further characterized that the average size of the synthesized nanoparticles was 9.5 ± 1.2 nm (Figure 1b).

nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images (Figure 1c) showed clear crystallinity and visible lattice fringes with interplane spacings of 0.212 and 0.191 nm, corresponding to the (111) and (200) planes of FCC PtPd-HEA.

nodes.characterization_summary: PtPd-HEA shows concentric diffraction rings with bright discrete spots confirming FCC polycrystalline structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The polycrystallinity feature of PtPd-HEA was further confirmed by the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) (Figure 1d) in which the concentric diffraction rings with bright discrete diffraction spots were clear evidence for the FCC structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: Lattice strain observed in (111) plane of PtPd-HEA. Compressive strain of (111) plane for PtPd-HEA is 5.8% and for PtPdRu-HEA is 3.1%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The fast Fourier transform (FFT) pattern and the geometric phase analysis (GPA) strain diagram corresponding to the (111) plane (Figure 1e) visually indicate the occurrence of lattice strain in PtPd-HEA.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt, Pd, Co, Ni, Cu uniformly distributed in PtPd-HEA nanoparticles. Atomic ratio Pt:Pd:Co:Ni:Cu = 15:25:18:18:24.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) elemental mapping (Figure 1f) shows that Pt, Pd, Co, Ni, and Cu in PtPd-HEA are uniformly distributed in the nanoparticles.

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomic ratio of Pt:Pd:Co:Ni:Cu in PtPd-HEA is 14:20:20:20:26.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Quantitative analysis using STEM-energy dispersive spectroscopy (STEM-EDS) and inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) (Figure S2 and Tables S1, S2) reveal a consistent atomic ratio of each metal element in PtPd-HEA.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt 4f binding energy: PtPd-HEA 70.73 eV, PtPdRu-HEA 70.56 eV (vs Pt metal 71.20 eV). Pd 3d shows same trend. Co 2p and Cu 2p shift to higher energy, Ni 2p to lower energy in PtPdRu-HEA vs PtPd-HEA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: compared with metallic Pt (71.20 eV), the binding energy of Pt 4f in PtPd-HEA (70.73 eV) and in PtPdRu-HEA (70.56 eV) both shifted toward lower energy ... in PtPdRu-HEA, the XPS peak for Co 2p shifted toward higher energy ... Ni 2p shifted toward lower energy ... Cu 2p shifted toward higher energy

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L3-edge energy: Pt foil > PtPd-HEA > PtPdRu-HEA with decreasing white line intensity. Pd K-edge white line intensity: Pd foil > PtPd-HEA > PtPdRu-HEA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy of the Pt L3-edges follows the order Pt foil > PtPd-HEA > PtPdRu-HEA (Figure 2c) ... Figure 2d illustrates a decreasing trend in WL intensity at the Pd K-edge with the order Pd foil > PtPd-HEA > PtPdRu-HEA

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows differences in Pt-M bond distances and amplitudes in PtPd-HEA vs PtPdRu-HEA. WT-EXAFS indicates Ru weakens random distribution of Pt and changes TM environments.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FT-EXAFS spectral overlay of Pt elements in PtPd-HEA and PtPdRu-HEA revealed significant differences in the distance and amplitude of the absorber within the R range of 1.2–3.1 Å (Figure 2e).

nodes.characterization_summary: All catalysts exhibit relatively regular particle morphology. PtPd-HEA, PdRu-HEA, PtPdRu-HEA particles slightly smaller than PtRu-HEA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Field emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM) shows that all catalysts exhibit a relatively regular particle morphology with the size of PtPd-HEA, PdRu-HEA, and PtPdRu-HEA being slightly smaller than that of PtRu-HEA (Figure S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: PtPd-HEA shows Co-O and Ni-O vibration peaks from open circuit potential. Peaks shift positively with applied potential indicating water dissociation at Co/Ni sites. Enhanced response at 1550 cm⁻¹ and new peak at 1600 cm⁻¹ indicate water splitting.
nodes.evidence_snippet: in situ Raman spectra ... revealing characteristic peaks corresponding to Co-O and Ni-O bonds. Notably, vibration peaks associated with Ni-O and Co-O bonds are observed even in the absence of an applied potential ... slight positive shift in the Co-O bond and a pronounced positive shift in the Ni-O bond ... enhanced response at approximately 1550 cm⁻¹, along with the emergence of a new characteristic peak at around 1600 cm⁻¹

nodes.characterization_summary: PtPd-HEA shows peaks at 1060 cm⁻¹ (OH⁻), 2960 cm⁻¹ (OH_ad), faint peak near 2100 cm⁻¹ (Pt/Pd-H) with increasing potential. Red shift in 3000-3500 cm⁻¹ range indicates strong *H₂O adsorption.
nodes.evidence_snippet: in situ FTIR spectra of PtPd-HEA. The peaks observed at approximately 1060 cm⁻¹ and 2960 cm⁻¹ are attributed to OH⁻ and OH_ad respectively. Furthermore, a faint peak is detected near 2100 cm⁻¹ ... significant red shift of the peaks within the 3000-3500 cm⁻¹ range
